newsitem.title: UK: LME July option declaration uneventful for copper.
newsitem.headline: LME July option declaration uneventful for copper.

text.p: July traded options declarations on the London Metal Exchange (LME) passed smoothly, particularly in copper, where the July date settled between strikes, traders said.
In aluminium and in lead there were some partial declarations, but in the other contracts there was nothing of note.
"It was all pretty mundane this time around, especially as there is automatic declarations in place now," one trader said.
In copper, the declaration proved to be a damp squib, as the July price for most of the morning settled in the no-mans-land between the $2,500 and $2,550 strikes.
"It passed uneventfully...after trading as high as 40 percent (volatility) recently it all came to nothing," another trader said.
At one stage during the morning, some ten minutes before the declaration process, the copper price did show signs of easing back to levels where July could have been straddling $2,500.
But for most of the pre-market July was around $2,525/30, so the calls at $2,500 were all in-the-money.
Latest clearing house data showed that there were some 927 lots of contracts open at this level.
Some traders said the market may have overdone its concern and uncertainty over the July declarations.
"There was not really a large open interest to worry about," one said.
Open interest at $2,550 was just under 500 lots, but by yesterday it became increasingly unlikely that the larger open interest strikes at $2,600 and $2,650 were going to be in play.
In aluminium, there were partial declarations of the $1,600 calls, which were brought into the frame when the underlying market moved higher on Tuesday afternoon, traders said.
"It (July) sat on the $1,600 level all morning, basically," a trader said.
Open interest at the $1,600 strike was some 1,300 lots of calls.

In lead, the rise in the underlying market meant that some of the $625 calls were declared, but the puts were largely abandoned, others said. Open interest for both the calls and the puts at this strike was 50 contracts.
In zinc, meanwhile, the underlying market's recent meteoric rise to the highest levels for nearly seven years resulted took the July date to near $1,450, where there were no strikes.
All the calls at and under $1,400 were declared, while all the puts were abandoned.
